transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-06 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Sparrow Head of Data), Evan Holt (Sparrow Security Eng), Jasmine Cole (Platform Lead)

Summary (auto): quick intake on compliance and deployment; customer mainly concerned about PHI residency, KMS, and fine-grained auditability

[00:00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round-robin, then we'll jump into your security questions.
[00:00:08] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here. We're responsible for data platform and compliance at Sparrow. Looking forward.
[00:00:12] Evan Holt: Evan, security engineer — I'll be focused on encryption, logs, SIEM, that sort of thing.
[00:00:17] Marco Diaz: Marco from Redwood SE. I'll cover technical fit questions and KMS/ops.
[00:00:24] Lena Park: Great. To set expectations — today is discovery. We'll cover SOC2/ISO posture, SSO options, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/BYOK, and retention. If anything else, shout out.

[00:02:05] Priya Nair: Our primary constraint is PHI. We need to know if Redwood Hosted can be used or if we must go Dedicated/Private. Also audit trails for access to PHI have to be tamper-evident.
[00:02:18] Lena Park: Understood. Short answer: Hosted is often fine with contract controls and SOC2, but for PHI many customers pick Dedicated or Private for VPC and stronger isolation — particularly if you want customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll get into specifics.

[00:04:10] Evan Holt: Can you run through your KMS options? We need BYOK and an HSM backed flow — keys never leave our control.
[00:04:18] Marco Diaz: Yup. Redwood integrates with AWS KMS and GCP KMS today; Dedicated and Private offer BYOK where you supply and control the key material. For HSM we have guidance for integrating with external HSMs — note that full HSM attestation may require Private deployment in some cases. Sometimes customers mix: use Hosted for non-PHI workloads and Dedicated with BYOK for PHI.
[00:05:00] Jasmine Cole: If we choose Dedicated, what's the lead time and what parts are configurable? Like can we pin model versions and control kernel selection?
[00:05:10] Lena Park: Yes, you can pin model versions, configure rollout policies, and set autoscaling/burst rules. Lead time depends on capacity commitments — ballpark 4–8 weeks for provisioned Dedicated clusters after contract.

[00:06:42] Priya Nair: SOC2 — do you have Type II? Any ISO 27001? We need to see the report and scope.
[00:06:50] Marco Diaz: Redwood currently maintains SOC2 Type II for the hosted control plane and can share the report under NDA. ISO 27001 is on our roadmap and we can share the timeline. I'll include a short matrix showing in-scope systems.

[00:08:20] Evan Holt: Audit logs — our requirement is full fidelity: who, what, when, and original request metadata. We need to ingest into Splunk and retain for 7 years for some records. Is that supported?
[00:08:32] Marco Diaz: Audit logs capture token-level request metadata, model, route, timestamps, IP, and agent. Logs can be exported to your SIEM via secure delivery (S3 push, syslog, or direct webhook). Retention depends on deployment: Hosted retains a default window for logs but we can set export to your long-term store. For Dedicated/Private you control retention and can ship to your S3 buckets for 7+ years.

[00:10:55] Priya Nair: Good — tamper-evident is important. Do you support immutable log stores or ledgering?
[00:11:02] Marco Diaz: We don't currently provide a native blockchain ledger, but we support write-once S3 buckets with versioning/immutability settings and can integrate with third-party WORM solutions. We'll document options.

[00:12:50] Speaker 1 (Evan?): I heard mention of KV cash — sorry — KV cache? How does caching affect PHI?
[00:12:58] Marco Diaz: Right, KV cache meaning the model key-value cache. By default we isolate KV caches per customer/session; for PHI you'd want to disable prefix caching or ensure caches are ephemeral and encrypted. For Dedicated/Private you can control cache lifetimes and disable cross-tenant caches.

[00:15:20] Jasmine Cole: SSO: we use Okta with SAML + SCIM for provisioning. Do you support that and group sync for RBAC mapping?
[00:15:29] Lena Park: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles and apply least-privilege. We'll share the SCIM schema and sample mapping.

[00:16:40] Priya Nair: For RBAC we need auditability of role changes and an approval workflow. Does Redwood keep change history?
[00:16:47] Marco Diaz: Yes, every admin action (role assignment, policy change) is logged with actor, timestamp, and diff. Those logs are part of the audit stream you can export. Approval workflows — we integrate with ticketing systems via webhooks; some customers layer in internal change controls.

[00:18:55] Evan Holt: Encryption at rest — is everything encrypted by default? What algorithms? Do you rotate keys?
[00:19:03] Marco Diaz: At-rest encryption is AES-256 by default. For Hosted we manage key rotation but can support customer-initiated rotation with BYOK on Dedicated/Private. TLS 1.2+/1.3 in transit. For BYOK we support key rotation semantics and CRLs via your KMS — we provide guidance for zero-downtime rotation if you're pinning model versions.

[00:20:45] Lena Park: Quick question — any regulatory constraints beyond HIPAA that we should be aware of? Data residency?
[00:20:52] Priya Nair: We need all PHI to stay in region (US east) and not cross into any non-US region. Also some records have a 7-year retention requirement.

[00:21:12] Marco Diaz: For residency we can route requests to US regions and for Dedicated/Private you can run entirely in your VPC in the region. We'll note region locking and model locality caveats in the follow-up doc.

[00:23:40] Jasmine Cole: Is there a way to mask PHI before it hits Redwood? We might pre-tokenize or scrub certain fields.
[00:23:47] Marco Diaz: Yes, customers often pre-process to remove or pseudonymize PHI. Redwood also supports input redaction rules on the client side and a configurable encryption-in-flight layer for certain fields. We'll add examples.

[00:25:10] Priya Nair: How about security assessments and penetration tests? We may require periodic pen tests and/or an on-site review.
[00:25:18] Lena Park: We run annual third-party pentests and can provide executive summaries. For on-site reviews we have an enterprise process; Private deployments are friendlier to that model. We'll include the pentest cadence and contact points.

[00:27:05] Evan Holt: For SIEM ingestion, what's the event format? JSON? Do you support Common Event Format or CEF for Splunk?
[00:27:13] Marco Diaz: We export JSON by default, and can provide CEF/CEF-like mappings. If you need log forwarding with specific fields, our team will work on a schema to match Splunk ingestion pipelines.

[00:29:00] Priya Nair: Are there any operational features for rollback and canary during model updates — we need safe rollouts for PHI-sensitive models.
[00:29:07] Lena Park: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B testing, automatic fallbacks, and model pinning. You can configure percentage rollouts and automatic rollback on error thresholds. We'll include an example config.

[00:31:20] Jasmine Cole: Cost and latency tradeoffs — if we go Dedicated in-region, what's the expected latency for 4k token prompts?
[00:31:30] Marco Diaz: It depends on model family and instance type; dedicated clusters aimed at low-latency inference can hit sub-200ms per token for shorter contexts on optimized kernels. We'll run bench tests with your sample workload to give realistic numbers.

[00:33:55] Speaker 2 (Priya): On data retention, we want short-term ephemeral storage for inference traces (90 days) but long-term for audit logs (7 years). Can you split that?
[00:34:03] Marco Diaz: Yes, telemetry/inference traces and raw inputs can be configured separately from audit logs. For Hosted we have defaults (90 days), but for Dedicated/Private you own long-term retention. We'll document configuration options.

[00:36:40] Evan Holt: Any concerns about model caching leaking PHI across requests?
[00:36:48] Marco Diaz: We isolate caches per tenant and implement strict eviction. For maximal safety we can disable caching for endpoints that handle PHI or ensure caches are encrypted and routinely purged.

[00:38:15] Lena Park: Quick recap before Qs — main asks: you need SOC2 artifacts, KMS/BYOK clarity, SIEM export schema, retention mapping, and a bench run. We'll prioritize those.

[00:39:02] Priya Nair: Sounds good. One last question: What SLA/incident transparency do you provide? We need post-mortems and exposure reports.
[00:39:12] Marco Diaz: For Dedicated customers we offer SLA-backed uptime and incident op notes. We provide incident summaries and post-mortems for significant outages. We can map required report fields for your SOC/HIPAA audits.

[00:41:00] Jasmine Cole: Could you also include cost implications of long-term log retention? Storing 7 years of high-fidelity logs will be material.
[00:41:08] Lena Park: We'll include a cost estimate and suggested lifecycle (hot/warm/cold) to reduce expense.

[00:42:30] Evan Holt: Ok, next steps then?
[00:42:34] Lena Park: We'll send SOC2 and the security whitepaper (Lena). Marco will send KMS/BYOK integration notes and the SIEM event schema. We'll schedule the SE bench — Jasmine to share throughput targets and example dataset. Expect all materials in the next week.

[00:43:10] Priya Nair: Thanks. We'll review and align on a pilot once we get the docs.
[00:43:18] Lena Park: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive.
[00:43:25] Meeting end.
